### C1 details

`upload_dataset_directory` previously caught raised exceptions but ignored the return value from `upload_dataset(...)`. The underlying `_upload()` returns `""` on every internal failure (HF_TOKEN missing, 401/403, verification mismatch, caught HF API exception). So a real silent-failure path was reported as success.

After the fix:
- **Default mode (`fail_soft=False`):** `ret == ""` → `RuntimeError(f"upload_dataset returned '' for {f} -> {path_in_repo}; HF Hub upload failed silently ...")` is raised. Calling script exits non-zero. CLAUDE.md Upload Policy ("exits non-zero on upload failure") is now ACCURATE.
- **Soft mode (`fail_soft=True`):** `ret == ""` → log to stderr, skip the file from the returned list, continue to next file.

Fix is at the helper layer only (per round-2 brief: do NOT modify `_upload()` itself — out-of-scope, would touch existing infrastructure used by other callers).

### C2 details

The 4 placeholders (`dpo_midtrain/dpo_evil_correct.jsonl`, `dpo_evil_wrong.jsonl`, `dpo_good_correct.jsonl`, `dpo_good_wrong.jsonl`) were uploaded by the round-1 §3 end-to-end smoke when `data/generated/wrong_answers_*.jsonl` was absent from the worktree (→ 0 QA pairs → 0-byte outputs). Smoke verified the upload pathway, but leaving 0-byte files in a public dataset repo is misleading.

**Disposition:** deleted via `HfApi.create_commit(operations=[CommitOperationDelete(...)])`. Commit message: `[#293 C2] Delete 4 zero-byte placeholder JSONLs from §3 round-1 smoke`. Verified: `dpo_midtrain/` now has 0 files. Future production runs (with real `wrong_answers_*.jsonl` inputs) will populate the bucket correctly. No fix needed to `build_dpo_midtrain_data.py` itself — its dependency on `wrong_answers_*.jsonl` is by design.

### C3 details

Template (`.claude/skills/clean-results/template.md` lines 104-110) ships with a multi-line `<!-- ... -->` block containing a stub `![{{...}}](...)` for an optional secondary figure. The §1 caption walker's `html_comment_re = re.compile(r"^\s*<!--.*-->\s*$")` only matched single-line comments, so the embedded image was treated as a real figure and the walker demanded a caption that didn't exist.

Fix: scrub multi-line `<!--.*?-->` spans from the Results block via `re.sub(..., re.DOTALL)` BEFORE the line-walker runs. Single-line HTML-comment handling preserved for backward compat with the existing `test_caption_html_comment_only_fails` legacy fixture.

### Section 2 — Closing an issue auto-routes to Archived

**Goal.** When a user runs `gh issue close <N>`, automatically move the issue to the `Archived` project-board column. Symmetric reopen: strip `status:archived`, restore `status:proposed`.

**Architecture decision.** v2 splits this into a **NEW** `.github/workflows/project-archive-on-close.yml` rather than extending `project-sync.yml`. Reason: PAT-driven label mutations re-enter the same `project-sync-${N}` concurrency group; with `cancel-in-progress: true`, the `closed` run could be cancelled mid-loop by its own label-event children. New workflow uses its own `archive-on-close-${N}` group with `cancel-in-progress: false` — no race.

**Sticky labels (USER DECISIONS, binding):**
- **`status:done-experiment` / `status:done-impl` are sticky.** Closing a Done issue is a NO-OP on labels. Only `gh issue edit --remove-label status:done-*` un-Dones an issue.
- **`clean-results:*` priority labels are sticky.** Closing a promoted clean-result keeps it in its `Useful` / `Not useful` / `Awaiting promotion` column. Consistent with `gh_project.py:PRIORITY_LABELS` — the existing routing layer would have done this anyway, but the workflow short-circuits to keep labels themselves stable.

**Token-scope precheck.** A read+write probe at the top of the workflow (using `gh issue view` + an idempotent `gh issue edit --add-label` of an already-applied label) hard-fails with a useful message if `PROJECT_TOKEN` lacks `issues:write`. Replaces the silent `403 || true` failure mode.
